data.long_meaning: From the Welsh word ‘clud’ meaning ‘meadow’ or ‘open land’. In ancient Wales, the name Clywd was given to children born on hills or in meadows. The name Clywd carries the meaning “Hill, meadow, open land” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Clywd usually hope their child will grow to embody hill, meadow, open land and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Clywd is rooted in the ancient Celtic belief that nature held great spiritual power. The name represents a connection to the natural world and can be seen as a reminder of the divine presence in all things. It may also be a symbol of spiritual growth and expansion, like the open land or meadow that nurtures and strengthens those who inhabit it. In Christianity, this name can be seen as a reminder of the boundless love and grace of God, who nurtures and protects all his children, like a meadow that fosters and provides for its inhabitants.
